attempts.sql: SELECT s.symbol_id, COUNT(*)::INTEGER AS method_count FROM code.symbols s JOIN code.files f ON f.file_id = s.file_id WHERE s.kind = 'class' AND f.is_test = FALSE AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM code.symbols m WHERE m.file_id = s.file_id AND m.kind = 'method' AND m.qualname LIKE s.qualname || '.%' AND m.line_start >= s.line_start AND m.line_end <= s.line_end AND m.qualname NOT LIKE s.qualname || '.%.%') GROUP BY s.symbol_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20 ORDER BY method_count DESC, s.symbol_id ASC

request:
Which classes in the non-test code define at least 20 methods directly in their own body? Count every method definition separately (a property getter and its setter count as two; inherited methods and methods of nested classes do not count). Return each class's symbol ID and its method count, largest count first, ties broken by symbol ID alphabetically.

Requested output columns: symbol_id (string), method_count (integer). Order the rows as the question asks.
explanation: Counts method symbols whose qualname is a direct child of each class (one dot deeper, no further nesting) and whose definition lines fall within the class body, restricting to classes in non-test files. Classes with at least 20 such direct methods are returned, ordered by count descending then symbol ID.
sql: SELECT s.symbol_id, COUNT(*)::INTEGER AS method_count FROM code.symbols s JOIN code.files f ON f.file_id = s.file_id WHERE s.kind = 'class' AND f.is_test = FALSE AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM code.symbols m WHERE m.file_id = s.file_id AND m.kind = 'method' AND m.qualname LIKE s.qualname || '.%' AND m.line_start >= s.line_start AND m.line_end <= s.line_end AND m.qualname NOT LIKE s.qualname || '.%.%') GROUP BY s.symbol_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 20 ORDER BY method_count DESC, s.symbol_id ASC
